item.title: Geer: Re-seat the Marion Square Commission to restore public trust
item.description: Charleston is a city built in layers. item.title: Commission pushes for new city archaeologist to protect Charleston
item.description: Influential Charleston historian Harlan Greene, who chairs the city of Charleston’s Commission on History, on Tuesday told members of city council that they needed to do more to protect and preserve the Holy City. item.title: Year of the Horse: Celebrate lunar new year on Feb. 14
item.description: The second annual lunar new year celebration returns to Charleston on Feb. 14. This year’s celebration takes place from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m at Storehouse 9 at 2154 Noisette Blvd. in the Navy Yard. item.title: Evette to get big GOP endorsement from incumbent governor
item.description: S.C. Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette today is expected to get a big endorsement in an effort to break away from a pack of Republicans who want to be the state’s next governor. The post Evette to get big GOP endorsement from incumbent governor appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Our View: Protect Charleston by hiring archaeologist
item.description: There’s been a century-long clash in Charleston between the past and present that has become grittier in recent years. The zeal to make a buck competes with Charleston‘s legacy to preserve its buildings, character and history. item.title: Weekend offers 2 chances to flip open binoculars for birds
item.description: As thousands of camo-attired visitors flock to Charleston for the annual Southeastern Wildlife Exposition, state officials are encouraging area residents to get outside to count birds. The S.C. Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR) is conducting two bird surveys Feb. 13 through Feb. 16.
